front_chapters.title: PoC scope and acceptance
paragraphs: This proof of concept (PoC) tests Agent 365 controls against named test agents.
The kit contains source code, infrastructure templates, procedures, test data, queries, and an evidence recorder.
No customer tenant result is included.
The customer must approve each deployment, policy change, external connection, and test scope.

sections.title: Execution sequence
steps: Approve the scope, licences, roles, preview access, data locations, cost limit, and evidence location.
Install the kit and complete its local checks.
Prepare the dedicated identities, devices, provider accounts, synthetic files, and optional Azure resources.
Deploy each agent through its platform chapter. Complete ONB-01 through ONB-10.
Resolve any required onboarding blocker before claiming complete agent coverage.
Apply the Microsoft 365 and Entra procedures. Run M365 and ENTRA cases.
Apply the approved Defender and network procedures. Run DEF, MDE, MDCA, DFC, and GSA cases.
Apply the Purview procedures and run the approved PUR cases.
Connect the required investigation data. Run SENT and COP cases.
Run RSP cases after the required identity, action, and incident evidence exists.
Review acceptance and measured value with the customer.
Complete final cleanup only after all dependent cases finish.
notes: Restore temporary policy changes after each case.
Keep shared test agents and resources until every case that needs those objects is complete.
Destructive case cleanup belongs at that object's final use, not automatically after its first test.
Use separate evidence stores when the approved scope or catalogue changes.
Catalogue acceptance does not make the unsupported OpenAI connector available.

sections.title: Required demonstrations

rows: Registration, identity, authenticated use, and supported controls.
Hosting, publication, identity, and explicit Agent 365 telemetry.
Deployment, provider authorization, and actual interaction evidence.
Model execution, explicit instrumentation, and service-side telemetry.
Provider inventory synchronization and supported management actions.
Preview workspace connection and inventory synchronization.
Record the unsupported connector request. Use a separate SDK demonstration.
Local discovery and separately configured endpoint controls.

notes: The group names describe this PoC. They do not replace product classifications.
A missing feature remains a gap. Another integration does not prove the missing feature.

sections.title: Approve the test plan
steps: Copy config\poc-plan.example.json to an approved location outside the repository.
Replace each placeholder with the approved test value.
Record the tenant, cloud, region, users, devices, resource groups, agent aliases, and owners.
Record the approved cost limit and stop time.
Review the required flag for each catalogue case.
Approve optional preview tests separately.
Set target times before execution. Do not use measured times as retrospective targets.
Record the approval reference and the evidence reviewer.
notes: Keep actual tenant identifiers and approval records outside the source repository.
If a required feature is absent, record BLOCKED. Do not change the result to PASS.

sections.title: Apply acceptance rules
items: Run both the positive phase and the negative phase for each case.
Record the actual service decision and the actual action result.
Keep policy mode, scope, identity, timestamps, and correlation evidence.
Report required and optional cases separately.
Report approved exclusions with their original and revised denominators.
Keep local simulation results separate from live product results.
Keep a blocked case in the original denominator.
notes: A screenshot of a configured policy does not prove enforcement.
A model refusal does not prove that a security service blocked the request.
An empty query result does not prove that the agent performed no action.

sections.title: Assign operators

rows: Approve scope, sequence, cost, stop conditions, and acceptance.
Check licences, agent inventory, deployment scope, and consent.
Check identity objects, permissions, Conditional Access, and access expiry.
Prepare the Copilot Studio environment and connector policies.
Approve resources, roles, networking, model quota, and cleanup.
Prepare Defender, endpoint, network, and Sentinel controls.
Prepare Purview labels, policies, search, retention, and evidence access.
Compare artifacts with criteria and approve the final result.

notes: A responsibility is not an Entra role name.
Use the product role required by the relevant procedure.
Activate elevated roles only for the approved operation.

sections.title: Prepare isolation
steps: Use a dedicated evaluation tenant where possible.
Create named test users, test groups, and test devices.
Create a dedicated Power Platform environment and a dedicated Azure resource group.
Use separate provider accounts or workspaces for external agents.
Record all existing policy settings before changes.
Check policy assignments for production users and devices.
Stop if a change cannot remain within the approved scope.
Use a disposable tenant for a documented tenant-wide blocking demonstration.
notes: Do not connect production mailboxes, customer sites, or enterprise messaging to the test agents.
Do not disable a production protection to make a test succeed.

sections.title: Prepare synthetic data
steps: Inspect each file in fixtures.
Copy the public procedure and restricted record to the approved test location.
Use the DOCX copies for Office and SharePoint sensitivity-label tests. Use the TXT copies for the custom runtime.
Apply the test sensitivity label through the supported product procedure.
Create separate allowed and denied test accounts.
Share each test file only with the intended test identities.
Record the access grants before agent execution.
Use the untrusted instruction only in the isolated test.
notes: The fixture text does not create a Microsoft Purview label. The supplied DOCX files are also unlabeled.
Keep labeled test copies outside the repository. Never overwrite the clean fixture with protected customer content.
The untrusted instruction is not a guaranteed detector trigger.
Use the official harmless demonstration when the endpoint procedure requires that demonstration.

sections.title: Set stop conditions
items: Stop if a test affects a production identity, device, resource, or agent.
Stop if an agent reads real restricted data.
Stop if the selected policy scope differs from the approved scope.
Stop if a licence, consent, or required feature is absent.
Stop at the approved cost limit or end time.
Record the cause and preserve evidence before cleanup.

sections.title: Get the repository
steps: Install Git, Python 3.12, Node.js 24, and Azure CLI.
Install Bicep 0.46.1 for the local infrastructure checks.
Authenticate to GitHub with an account that can read the repository.
Clone the repository.
Open a PowerShell session in the repository root.
Read the source files before execution.
sections.code:
git clone https://github.com/oguzhanf/agent365-security-poc.git
Set-Location .\agent365-security-poc
python --version
node --version
az bicep install --version v0.46.1

sections.title: Run local checks
paragraphs: The evidence recorder uses the Python standard library.
The document build uses the pinned npm dependencies.
Runtime dependencies are separate from document dependencies.
notes: These checks do not authenticate to a tenant.
These checks do not prove a Microsoft security control.

sections.title: Use the package files

rows: Outbound-only custom model agent and explicit SDK instrumentation.
Foundry hosted model agent and explicit SDK instrumentation.
Bedrock infrastructure and Claude Managed Agents lifecycle code.
Local evidence records and acceptance reports.
Immutable references to official sample code.

notes: Keep evidence, credentials, and populated configuration files outside the repository.
The GitHub workflow checks source files. It does not deploy resources or set tenant policies.

sections.title: Use the correct identifier

rows: The process or service that executes the agent.
The code that controls model calls, tool calls, state, and execution limits.
The Entra application object used to create related agent identities.
The application identifier of the blueprint. This is not its object ID.
The application identifier of the agent identity.
The directory object identifier used for object management and role assignment.
A separate account used by supported agent-user experiences.
The accountable person assigned to the agent.
The import of agent records from a connected platform.
Events or traces emitted during agent execution.
A control decision that permits or prevents a selected action.

notes: Record object IDs and application IDs in separate fields.
Do not substitute one identifier because both values use GUID format.

sections.title: Start an evidence store
steps: Select an approved local evidence directory outside the repository.
Apply access controls to the directory.
Use a new directory for each approved execution scope.
Initialize the store with the complete catalogue.
Keep the catalogue unchanged for that execution.
notes: The command does not create a product result.
The tool requires local atomic file operations. Do not use a network share as its working store.

sections.title: Execute one case
steps: Select the case and confirm its prerequisites.
Record the agent alias and the actual identity in the protected evidence.
Capture the initial policy mode, scope, and resource state.
Run the positive phase and save the service decision.
Run the negative phase and save the service decision.
Check the actual action result after each phase.
Save sanitized artifacts under unique filenames in the evidence directory.
Record each phase with its correct evidence kind.
Restore the initial test state.
Ask the reviewer to compare the artifacts with the pass criteria.
notes: Use one fixed agent alias for both phases of a case.
For a comparison case, use one fixed test-set alias and identify its members in the artifacts.
Do not overwrite a recorded artifact. Add a new artifact for a rerun.

sections.title: Record a result
paragraphs: Replace CASE-ID with the actual catalogue ID.
Use PASS only after the artifact proves the stated criterion.
The example filenames are placeholders for actual sanitized product evidence.
sections.code:
python -m poc_evidence record --evidence-dir $Evidence --scenario CASE-ID --agent CPS-01 --phase positive --result PASS --reason "The approved action succeeded." --evidence-kind live_product --artifact positive.txt
python -m poc_evidence record --evidence-dir $Evidence --scenario CASE-ID --agent CPS-01 --phase negative --result PASS --reason "The protected action was denied." --evidence-kind live_product --artifact negative.txt
notes: Use local_simulation for runtime unit tests or offline demonstrations.
The recorder stores operator assertions. The recorder cannot determine whether an artifact came from a live service.
File hashes detect later changes. They do not certify artifact authenticity.

sections.title: Record a blocked case
sections.code: python -m poc_evidence record --evidence-dir $Evidence --scenario CASE-ID --agent CPS-01 --phase positive --result BLOCKED --reason "The required feature is absent." --evidence-kind live_product
notes: Record the missing feature, licence, permission, connector, or fixture.
Do not use NOT_APPLICABLE to hide a failed requirement.
Record an approved exclusion only after the customer changes the scope.

sections.title: Review acceptance
sections.code:
python -m poc_evidence verify --evidence-dir $Evidence --catalogue .\catalogue\scenarios.json
python -m poc_evidence report --evidence-dir $Evidence --catalogue .\catalogue\scenarios.json --format text
notes: Report exit code 1 means that original catalogue acceptance is not achieved.
Exit code 2 identifies an input, storage, concurrency, or integrity error.
Keep an approved archive of the evidence after review.
The recorder does not sign evidence or prevent an authorized writer from replacing the store.

sections.title: Measure elapsed time
steps: Copy config\measurement-template.json to the protected evidence location.
Use UTC timestamps for every start and end event.
Measure discovery time from agent creation to the correct inventory entry.
Measure revocation time from the approved block to a denied new request.
Measure alert time from the test action to the matching alert.
Measure investigation time from incident opening to confirmed identity and action.
Compare each measurement with the target approved before execution.
notes: Some block modes do not generate an alert. Use the documented decision record instead.
A cached token can delay access removal. Record token acquisition time and the new-session result.
Separate product propagation time from operator time.

sections.title: Measure coverage
items: Count inventoried agents against the known test inventory.
Count correctly attributed identities against the selected identity tests.
Count policy denials against attempted prohibited actions on supported paths.
Count complete investigations with identity, owner, action, and affected resource.
Report unknown, unsupported, blocked, and not-run cases separately.
notes: Do not compare different denominators without identifying the scope change.
Do not convert a preview result into a production availability claim.

sections.title: Issue the customer result
steps: List the agreed scope and the actual agent instances.
List the product versions, licence state, cloud, and preview features.
Attach the acceptance report and the evidence index.
Record each coverage gap and failed criterion.
Record residual access, remaining resources, and ongoing costs.
Obtain the customer decision for each unresolved item.

sections.title: Contain a test agent
steps: Identify the agent, identity, runtime, owner, and affected resource.
Preserve the current evidence before a destructive action.
Select the control that covers the actual execution path.
Block the Microsoft 365 entry point when that entry point is the target.
Disable or revoke the relevant identity access when that identity is the target.
Stop the dedicated runtime when continued execution is the target.
Apply the approved endpoint or provider control when execution occurs outside Microsoft 365.
Start a new request and confirm the selected action cannot occur.
notes: A registry block is not a universal runtime stop.
An identity change does not revoke an unrelated provider API key.
A disconnected inventory connector does not delete the provider agent.

sections.title: Restore service settings
steps: Restore each test policy to its recorded initial value.
Remove test assignments from users, devices, agents, and groups.
Remove test app installations and publication requests.
Revoke test consent and provider credentials that are no longer required.
Remove external platform connections after the evidence review.
Remove provider-side test agents through the provider procedure.
Remove test access packages and agent accounts where approved.
Remove endpoint test software only from the approved device.
Confirm that benign control actions work again.
notes: Review shared credentials and shared application objects before deletion.
Some preview objects cannot be deleted through the documented interface.
Record each residual object and its owner instead of claiming full cleanup.

sections.title: Remove Azure resources
paragraphs: Use scripts\azure\Remove-Lab.ps1 only for the dedicated tagged resource group.
The script does not remove tenant identities, provider agents, or Microsoft 365 policies.
steps: Compare the resource list with the approved deployment list.
Export approved evidence before resource deletion.
Run the cleanup script without its apply switch.
Inspect the exact deletion target and tag checks.
Obtain approval before the apply run.
Confirm that the approved resource IDs no longer exist.
Record the retained resource group and deployment history.
Review remaining usage and provider billing.

sections.title: Close the evidence record
steps: Run the evidence integrity check.
Save the final acceptance report in the protected location.
Record unresolved risks and residual resources.
Apply the approved retention period to the evidence archive.
Remove working copies at the approved expiry time.
Keep credentials and raw tenant evidence out of the GitHub repository.
